name: Community Water Development Fund

funder.name: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage (Ireland)

summary: Annual grants for Irish community and voluntary groups and environmental NGOs to improve water quality through river and wetland restoration, nature-based solutions and habitat works. The 2026 round closed in January 2026.

amount.note: Higher grant rates may be considered in certain circumstances

eligibility.rule: No excluded activities or costs, e.g. staff, overheads, insurance, income-generating or other RBMS-funded work
Any CWDF 2026 grant was fully paid before 5 December 2026
Submits no more than one application per organisation

documents: Constitution of the organisation or minutes of the most recent meeting
Most recent bank statement of the organisation
Quotations for each cost item, inclusive of VAT
Most recent audited or accountant-verified accounts or financial statement
Drawings, plans, specifications or photographs, if applicable
Planning permission conditions or notice of exemption from planning, if applicable
Current insurance policy, if physical work or voluntary labour is proposed
Evidence of tax clearance from Revenue for applications over €10,000

applicant_types.quote: Organisations based in the Republic of Ireland only Not-for-profit Community and Voluntary Groups Rural and Urban Networks Environmental Non-Government Organisations

geography.quote: The Fund is open to eligible applicants in the Republic of Ireland only.

window.quote: Closing Date Deadlines Applications via Online Portal www.lawaters.ie 11 Wednesday, 20 January 2026 at th 11:30pm

amount.quote: the minimum individual grant amount awarded under this scheme will be €5,000 up to a maximum of €40,000

administered_by.quote: provided by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage and administered by River Basin Management Service

co_finance_required.quote: It is not a grant condition, but it is recommended that applicants can demonstrate their ability to make a cash contribution

consortium_required.quote: Sole applicant organisations based in the Republic of Ireland only

eligibility.quote: Projects that solely benefit an individual. Teaching/staffing in schools. Travel, phone and transport costs except in exceptional circumstances. Equipment, unless directly associated with the project. Income generating projects. Overheads, ongoing running costs. Insurance. Accommodation and subsistence. Staff costs. Projects or expenditure funded under other RBMS fundingschemes.
To be eligible to apply, grants awarded under the CWDF 2026 scheme must be fully paid before 5th December 2026.
Only one application may be submitted per eligible organisation.
